> > sex <- as.numeric(pull.pheno(mymap.bwg3, "sex")=="M")
> >out.m <- scanone(subset(mymap.bwg3, ind=sex==1), addcovar=(sex==1))
> Error in checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  :
>   addcovar should be numeric
> In addition: Warning message:
> In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  :
>   Dropping 1 individuals with missing phenotypes.
> Why get the errror even I set the sex as numeric??
>

You're defining a vector 'sex' that has value 1 when the sex phenotype is "M" and 0 otherwise.
In the call to scanone(), subset(mymap.bwg3, ind=sex==1) is reducing the data set to just the males.
But in that case you shouldn't include sex as a covariate, and if you use (sex==1) as a covariate, that ends up being a logical vector of TRUEs and FALSEs, but you want just the numeric sex vector.

> so I did that instead
> >out.m <- scanone(subset(mymap.bwg3, ind=sex==1), addcovar=sex)
> Error in checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  :
>   Number of rows in additive covariates is incorrect
> In addition: Warning message:
> In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  :
>   Dropping 1 individuals with missing phenotypes.
>

You're subsetting the cross by sex==1, but you're including the full sex vector as a covariate, which is as long as the full cross rather than the cross subset to just the males.

>
> so I add the number of males to my ind argument
> out.m <- scanone(subset(mymap.bwg3, ind=sex==119), addcovar=sex)
> Error in subset.cross(mymap.bwg3, ind = sex == 119) :
>   Must retain at least one individual.

ind=sex==119 is saying subset to the individuals with sex == 119.
But sex has values 0 or 1, so there won't be any individuals with sex == 119.

>
> so I add the number of all individuals to my ind argument
> out.m <- scanone(subset(mymap.bwg3, ind=sex==119), addcovar=sex)
> Error in subset.cross(mymap.bwg3, ind = sex == 119) :
>   Must retain at least one individual.
> I tried many times always getting those 3 error messages.
>

If you want to do a genome scan in just the males:

    out.m <- scanone( subset(mymap.bwg3, ind=(sex==1) )

If you want to do a genome scan in just the females:

    out.f <- scanone( subset(mymap.bwg3, ind=(sex==0) )

If you want to do a scan with all individuals, using sex as an additive covariate:

    out.a <- scanone( mymap.bwg3, addcovar=sex )

If you want to do a scan with all individuals, using sex as an interactive covariate:

    out.i <- scanone( mymap.bwg3, addcovar=sex, intcovar=sex )

karl

> value, 63%, 10% and 5% if possible.

with plot.scanone, use arguments 'col' and 'lty' to change the color and
line type, respectively.

messages.body_plain:
> the issue now, when I did stepwise qtl for any of my analyzed traits
> the result of the first step of the analysis is not the same as

> scanone analysis. I understood from the book that both steps give the

> same out put.
> for many of the traits it give me only one qtl which is the one with
> the highest score, even though the scanone out put provide 3 or 2 qtl
> at least on of them is significant.

The first step of stepwiseqtl() is to chose the single highest peak from
scanone().

scanone() is always comparing a single-QTL model to the model with no QTL.
stepwiseqtl() is seeking to build a multiple-QTL model. Two QTL may look
important, individually, but it may be that once you account for the
first one, there is no longer evidence for the 2nd.

karl

>
> Also the first warning message is strange as the no of individuals is
> the same for the same analysis
> Warning messages:
> 1: In fitqtl(mymap.bwg28, qtl = outsw3, model = "normal", formula = y ~  :

> re-creating qtl object.
> 2: In fitqtlengine(pheno = pheno, qtl = qtl, covar = covar, formula =
> formula,  :
>   Dropping 1 individuals with missing phenotypes.
>

There is one individual who is missing the phenotype, which causes these
warnings.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Droponemarker calls est.map without 'n.cluster'
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Droponemarker calls est.map without 'n.cluster'
messages.body_plain:
The n.cluster argument in est.map() parallelizes on the chromosome level. Since droponemarker() considers a single chromosome, it wouldn't really help. What's needed would be to parallelize on the marker, in this line: https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/droponemarker.R#L80

I think the main way to speed it up is through by using a small number for maxit; you probably don't need to get a great map estimate in order to identify problem markers.

We've not yet implemented this in R/qtl2.

karl

messages.subject_clean: Basic request: genotype encoding and data format
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
first of all, plase excuse my question for being very basic.

I have genetic data of a F1 full sib progeny from heterozygous parents. The species is poplar. The markers are codominant, either SSR or SNP. The phase of the genotypes is unknown.

The diploid genotypes are scored be as follows
Markes   M1 M2 M3
Parent-1 AA AA AB
Parent-2 AB BC AC
----F1-1 AA AB AB
----F1-2 AB AC AC
----F1-3 AA AB BC
----F1-4 AB AC ...
and so on

This experimental design is usually analysed as BackCross population by Pseudo Test Cross Strategy. I have some previous experience with MapMaker.

I would like to analyse my data with R/QTL and R/ASMap. Thus I need to format them for importing in R as data.frame or cross object. I have nof found clear instruction in Vignette and I have not found an example of raw genotype table for BackCross populations. An appropriate "mapBCu" dataset is provided with the package, but I was not able to extract the raw genotypes as data.frame from the cross object.
Thus, I have tried several allele encoding schemes, but I always got the below error message when trying to open the data.frame with mstmap command.

-----------
> mstmap.data.frame(MyData, pop.type = "BC", dist.fun = "kosambi", trace = TRUE, as.cross = TRUE)

Error in mstmap.data.frame(MyData, pop.type = "BC", dist.fun = "kosambi",  :
  Non-allowable allele encodings in DH marker set
-----------
It seems that my data.frame is interpreted as DH population, despite of the argument pop.type = "BC".

Can anyone help me or provide an example of the right encoding for my data?

Many Thanks

Isacco Beritognolo
Italy
